_what: The writes a site's action rows may ask tool:keep-a-site-write for, by name. Each is one fixed statement and the values it takes, in parameter order ($1 is the first value): a caller sends a name and values only, never SQL. A value is text (at most `most` characters) or a list of texts (at most `most` of them); one not given is null, unless it is required. The statements are the ones a site's run-sql action rows sent (Nov 25 2026), changed only where the writer login may not do what they did: no RETURNING (the login cannot read the rows it adds), and the welcome stop through the owner's stop_welcome_series(token), so the login never reads a token.

site-lead._what: A lead from a site form (book a call): one statement of meaning lead, kept only when the email has an email's shape.
site-lead.sql: INSERT INTO statements (source, told, place, meaning, at, key, after) SELECT 'site-form', 'site-form:lead:' || $1, 'site-form', 'lead', now(), $1, jsonb_strip_nulls(jsonb_build_object('email', lower(trim($2::text)), 'name', nullif(trim($3::text), ''), 'self_reported', nullif(trim($4::text), ''), 'offer_id', $5::text, 'visitor', $6::text, 'touch_id', $7::text)) WHERE $2::text ~ '^[^[:space:]@]+@[^[:space:]@]+\.[^[:space:]@]+$'

site-checkout._what: One checkout a buyer started (a journey step), kept once per attempt: its key is the attempt, and a second keep of the same attempt keeps nothing. It is the statement the checkout row's run-sql `then` sent, without RETURNING (the writer login cannot read the rows it adds).
site-checkout.sql: INSERT INTO statements (source, told, place, meaning, at, key, after) VALUES ('site-checkout', 'site-checkout:checkout:' || $1, 'site-checkout', 'checkout', now(), $1, jsonb_strip_nulls(jsonb_build_object('attempt', $1::text, 'offer_id', $2::text, 'visitor', $3::text, 'touch_id', $4::text))) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING

site-visit._what: A visit a page tells the site of: kept only when the address it names is on the origin the request came from. It names what was told (site-visit:visit:<key>), as the lead does: statements.told is required, and the action row this came from left it out, so every visit it sent was refused (found by the writer proof on the live database, 12:33 PM CST Nov 25 2026).
site-visit.sql: INSERT INTO statements (key, source, told, place, meaning, after, at) SELECT $1, 'site-visit', 'site-visit:visit:' || $1, 'site-visit', 'visit', jsonb_build_object('href', $3::text, 'referrer', $4::text, 'visitor', $2::text), now() WHERE $5::text = $6::text

price-view._what: One view of each offer whose price a page showed, counted per offer and day; only offers that exist, at most 20 a time.
price-view.sql: INSERT INTO price_views (offer_id, day, views) SELECT id, (now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::date, 1 FROM offers WHERE id = ANY(($1::text[])[1:20]) ON CONFLICT (offer_id, day) DO UPDATE SET views = price_views.views + 1

welcome-series-stop._what: Stops the welcome emails of the token's address (the owner's stop_welcome_series, which matches the token and keeps the first stop), and answers the page to go to: stopped_path when the token matched, invalid_path when not.
welcome-series-stop.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN public.stop_welcome_series(coalesce($1::text, '')) THEN $2::text ELSE $3::text END AS goto
